title: Two R208 test titles assert the erased-pile behaviour R219 reversed
summary: In 178-played-item-and-erased-mods, the Slag Spewer test is titled "an erase paid as a COST still announces itself with info — Q3 is OPEN" and the Suppression Field test "... and the pile is untouched". Both titles state R208's held behaviour (a mod erased off a living host files nothing on the erased pile), which R219 reversed. Both bodies now assert the R219 behaviour: the erased mod is on the pile. The titles say the opposite of what the tests check.

title: A copy-layer test title still calls stripping a veto
summary: The 44-hybrids-ld-a test "R118: R62 suppression is a veto ABOVE copy" and its message "R62 sits ABOVE layer 0" describe R62's veto, which R328 reversed (stripping is applied in timestamp order). The test strips after the copy is made, so its assertions still hold under R328, but no test pins a copy that begins after a strip (see D-U16-6), and the title asserts superseded law.

title: A unit stripped by a continuous effect (Monke, Transmogrifant) keeps applying its own static abilities
summary: Transmogrifant and Monke make other units "lose all attributes and abilities", and R62 says a static is an ability, but static-vs-static resolves in one pass that skips only a holder with the one-time stamp. The verifier's probe measured a 1/1 token at 3/5 with Sandstone Defender under Transmogrifant, where the printed text gives 3/3. R62 justifies the one pass only by the mutual case (two Monkes); the one-sided case falls out of the same shortcut.

title: Tough augmented onto a printed-Balanced unit: the engine balances first, the Manual's "augmented onto" sentence doubles first
summary: Manual p.42: "if Tough is augmented onto a Balanced unit ... it will have its defense doubled, then its stats balanced." The engine (R19's own call: printed attributes before mod attributes) gives the reverse: the verifier's probe measured Child of Aether (2/0 Balanced) with a Tough augment at 2/4, where that sentence gives 2/2. The same answer's last sentence ("applied to") gives balanced, then doubled, so this waits on the owner's reading (D-U16-1).
